quotes.text: You can't install a physical firewall box in a data center you don't own. And even if you could, it wouldn't help because there's no single door to guard anymore.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains in plain terms why the cloud breaks the traditional perimeter firewall model.

quotes.text: Both directions need inspection. If a hacker gets into one workload, you don't want them roaming freely to others. That's how breaches spread.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes the case for inspecting east-west as well as north-south traffic.

quotes.text: A firewall only works if traffic actually passes through it. If you place it in the wrong spot, it might as well not exist.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A crisp reminder that network architecture matters as much as the firewall itself.

quotes.text: That's why deployment design matters just as much as the rules themselves. A perfect rule set means nothing if traffic can bypass the firewall entirely.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States a clear design principle for firewall deployments.

quotes.text: Premium adds TLS inspection, which decrypts encrypted traffic, inspects the contents and re-encrypts it before sending it on. That matters because most malicious traffic today hides inside encrypted connections
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains what TLS inspection does and why it matters.

takeaways: Azure Firewall is a fully managed, cloud-native firewall service with built-in high availability and autoscaling that inspects inbound, outbound and east-west traffic.
Basic, Standard and Premium SKUs add capabilities step by step, from IP and port filtering to threat intelligence in deny mode, web categories, TLS inspection, IDPS and URL filtering.

Traffic is only inspected if it passes through the firewall, so a hub-and-spoke design, correctly ordered NAT, network and application rules, and cost controls like the Log Analytics basic table plan matter as much as the SKU.
hook: Cloud networks have no single front door, so a physical firewall at the edge no longer protects your workloads. This episode is for Azure admins and anyone new to Azure networking, and explains what Azure Firewall does, how its SKUs, rules and hub-and-spoke placement work, and which setup to start with today.
